title: Exploring Mental Health Experiences Among Sexual Minority Women Intercollegiate Athletes in Canada
abstract: Sexual minority athletes face significant discrimination and barriers to participation in sports. For women athletes, the challenges are compounded by pervasive sexism. As a result, sexual minority women athletes endure unique, interconnected stressors that highlight the need for further study into their experiences. This qualitative study explores the mental health experiences of six sexual minority women competing in Canadian intercollegiate sport through conversational interviews. Reflexive thematic analysis revealed three interrelated themes: (a) navigating identity in sport, (b) sport as a context of support and psychological strain, and (c) strategies of resilience and resistance. Findings highlight the complex intersections of athletic identity, sexual orientation, and psychological well-being in competitive environments. The study emphasizes the need for inclusive, equity-driven support systems that affirm LGBTQIA+ athletes and offers implications for coaches, sport organizations, and mental health practitioners aiming to foster equity and inclusion in university sport.
